item.title: Man charged in relation to Co Monaghan fatal collision
item.description: Gardaí continue to investigate a fatal road traffic collision involving a HGV and a car on the N2 at Castleblayney, Co. Monaghan on Thursday, 18th December 2025. The road remains closed at this time while efforts are ongoing to safely remove the obstructing vehicle. The man in his 50s arrested in connection with this collision has since been charged and is due to appear before a special sitting of Monaghan District Court at 7:00pm this evening. Advertisement

item.title: Allianz to remain as GAA sponsor
item.description: The GAA has decided to continue their sponsorship relationship with Allianz. Allianz have been long term sponsors of the national football and hurling leagues. A number of county boards including Roscommon and Leitrim moved proposals to central council to remove Allianz as a sponsor. item.title: Man appears in court over death of woman in collision on the N2
item.description: A 56-year-old man has appeared in court tonight charged in relation to the death of Emma Mackeral. Ion Bucurica appeared at Monaghan District Court charged with dangerous driving causing the death of the Co Monaghan mother of two. The Romanian national who resides in France appeared in front of Judge Gerard Jones at a special sitting of Monaghan District Court over the alleged offence. Advertisement Inspector Damien Martin gave evidence of arrest, charge and caution at the brief hearing tonight.

item.title: Claim Jim Gavin controversy did not affect Jack Chambers job challenged
item.description: The Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers' claim the Jim Gavin controversy didn't affect the job he was doing is being shot down. Labour TD George Lawlor thinks it would impact on his job. It's after it was revealed in the party's review Minister Chambers knew of a potential issue with a tenant for Jim Gavin before he was chosen to run for the Presidency. Advertisement Deputy George Lawlor says there's no doubt it would affect his work. Advertisement

item.description: A local financial expert says Cavan Town is a great bustling business town especially during the festive season. Anna Smith from Farnham Financials says the important focus at this time of the year is shopping local and rightly so. She says it's important where possible to shop local which supports local and helps with the retention of jobs in your community. item.title: Local TD criticises government over unfunded blister packs
item.description: A Sinn Féin TD for Cavan-Monaghan, has slammed the government's failure to fund blister packs under the Community Pharmacy Agreement. Deputy Cathy Bennett has warned that from 1st January next year vulnerable patients will be hit with additional charges of up to 50 euro per month for blister packs to help manage their medicines. item.title: Wolves equal worst ever premier league start
item.description: Wolves equalled the lowest Christmas points tally in Premier League history after falling to a 10th straight defeat.
